title: Entropy-aware mini-windowing and kernel collocation to reduce embedding endpoint tail
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Embedding endpoint p99 remains high under mixed tenant workloads with heterogeneous request characteristics (short vs long context, high vs low token entropy). Existing mini-batching and kernel selection heuristics group requests based on sequence length and arrival window, but we see persistent tail spikes caused by: (1) batches that accidentally combine high-entropy vectors with low-entropy ones causing kernel execution variance; (2) frequent kernel context switches on pooled GPUs when request mixes change rapidly; (3) latency amplification from opportunistic coalescing that holds requests too long during bursty arrivals.\n\nGoal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 by 20-35% on average for production traffic across multi-tenant hosts without increasing p50 (>5%) or significantly increasing cost. Approach: introduce an \"entropy-aware mini-windowing\" pre-pass to ingress that computes a lightweight entropy/shannon-score proxy and groups requests into short windows optimized for kernel execution. Combine this with \"kernel collocation\": a scheduler hint that favors keeping similar kernel parameterizations on the same GPU to reduce warmup overhead and preemption. Add adaptive pacing to limit holding time for low-latency requests when coalescing benefit is marginal.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end p99 for embedding endpoint reduces by >=20% in A/B test vs baseline on representative production replay. 2) p50 change within +/-5%. 3) No user-facing errors introduced and SLO error budget usage does not increase. 4) Telemetry: kernel-switch-rate per-GPU drops by >=30% and entropy-bucket tail latency improvement visible in dashboard. 5) Feature gated and can be turned off per-tenant via runtime flag.
technical_design: Ingress pre-pass: compute a proxy entropy metric using normalized token unigram distribution sketch (fast approximate method implemented in C++ with SIMD). Tag each request with entropy_bucket: low/medium/high and length_bucket: short/medium/long. Mini-windowing: maintain three parallel short windows (10ms, 25ms, 50ms) with per-bucket thresholds; windows flush early if batch size or latency budget crossed. Scheduler: extend existing microbatch scheduler to accept kernel_collocation_hint derived from dominant entropy+length bucket for batch. Kernel collocation policy: prefer assignment to GPU lanes where last N batches used the same kernel parameterization (quantization kernel variant, sequence packing strategy). Pacing: dynamic hold limit that decays when observed benefit (tokens saved) falls below configured threshold.\n\nImplementation notes: avoid serialization bottleneck in pre-pass; run entropy sketch in ingress threadpool and keep tags compact. All changes behind runtime flags and feature flags per-cluster and per-tenant. Provide a graceful fallback path to current scheduler on failure.
experiments: 1) Offline replay: run production traffic replay across host fleet emulator with new pre-pass and collocation on/off to measure deterministic impact. 2) Canary: enable on 5% of traffic for non-critical tenants across two regions and monitor p99, p50, kernel-switch-rate, and CPU overhead on ingress nodes. 3) Stress tests: synthetic high-entropy burst tests to validate no regression in maximum latency or OOM behavior. 4) Compare with baseline microbatch parameters (current best known config) and with an aggressive coalescing ablation to measure trade-offs.
telemetry: New metrics: ingress_entropy_bucket_count{low,medium,high}, ingress_entropy_histogram, kernel_switches_per_gpu, kernel_collocation_ratio, hold_time_distribution, microwindow_flush_reasons, per-tenant_p99_by_entropy_bucket. Dashboards: entropy-tail-latency heatmap, kernel-switch trend, ingress CPU utilization. Alerts: p99 regression >10% for canary or kernel_switches_per_gpu increase >50%.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (local): unit and integration tests + perf bench. Phase 1 (replay): run offline replay for 72h and validate. Phase 2 (canary): 5% production traffic for two non-critical clusters, monitor for 24-72h. Phase 3 (ramped rollout): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with rollback gates at each step. All toggles controlled via runtime config and per-tenant flag. Post-rollout: automated regression check and hyperparameter autotune job scheduled after 1 week.
risks: 1) Entropy sketch CPU overhead could increase ingress node CPU leading to backpressure. 2) Collocation may cause hotspotting of kernels on GPUs if assignment not balanced. 3) Edge cases: tiny batches with mixed entropy could be harmed if held incorrectly. 4) Complexity increases scheduler maintainability. Mitigation: guardrails, CPU budget limits, fairness counters, fallback to existing scheduler when thresholds hit.
blockers: Need updated kernel-hotness telemetry from runtime team (ENG-298501) and a small sync with infra to add feature flag hooks to canary infra. Also require a review from security for new telemetry exposure (PII review).
